title: Need help using ai to build a bot to play against
author: Friendly_Bee_Gameco
selftext:
Hey gang - I have a strategy game I built it’s kind of like checkers with economy and engine building if you know what that is. It’s very deep and strategic. I used fable to make it into an app which was cake but now I’m trying to get fable to build a bot for me to play against and the bots are just terrible. 

I have it saving game logs to review and I’m basically playing a game and giving it feedback but I feel like this constant iteration isn’t helping it’s starting to go back and overwrite old rules it made and I feel like we’re stuck in a loop.

I had it do the thing where it simulated a bunch of games but that doesn’t work very well - two terrible players going against each other doesn’t teach you much. Now I’m kind of at a loss - how do I make a strong bot? Anybody have learnings from dealing with something similar?

comments.author: Correct_Emotion8437
comments.body:
I have made bots for a few standard games just for the fun of making bots.  I'd start out with making a rules based or deterministic bot.  Depending on your game, you might be able to make one that simulates the next X number of moves - a minimax bot.  If there is too much that depends on human decision or if there are different play styles and strategies, it can get really tricky.  

For fun on a simple game I tried training on a random bot like 20,000 games and there was almost no improvement - so even if you go that route you have to come up with a teacher.  I don't think it's feasible to record your own play - you need way more data.  I've had AI lie to me about exactly that - tell me all I need is a few hundred games and then I end up with crap.  But I was training on 10,000 games when I was using a teacher and I would get improvements - it would end up beating the teacher.

replies.author: Friendly_Bee_Gameco
replies.body:
Yea - I started deterministic but there was too much swirl (rewriting rules each time). Tried the look ahead bot but I think too many choices. Now we’ve established a baseline - new bot has to beat the old bot to advance. Trying to get it to do some local optimization and see if that helps

Agree that me playing games/games history is too slow so I’m hopeful this bot tournament style will show progress

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: if your using claude or somethin like that, create an ai vs ai game let it play, have claude or an ai review a log. Basic bots need reward signals and they make choice based of whats highest value. I made a basic mtg bot that way, it only goes so far but its a place to start.

replies.author: Friendly_Bee_Gameco
replies.body: Yea that’s where we are. At first it didn’t help so much but now we established a rule that changes only go into effect if the new bot beats the old bot - so now we’re doing a tournament to optimize. We’ll see if that helps

comments.author: IAmhowlshot
comments.body: what type of game is it? Perhaps you can look up some existing ai/bots that might be able to guide a scaffold for this?

replies.author: Friendly_Bee_Gameco
replies.body: That’s a good idea I’ll check for that. It’s kind of checkers style but you also are building a tableau of bonus actions that trigger depending on the tiles you step on - so it requires tactical positional thinking and long term engine planning simultaneously. The bot is good at tactics but crap at blending tactics and long term - which quite frankly is the hard part - it’s playing like a new-ish human player but I want it to be unbeatable so I can try to use it for gameplay analytics - recommending game improvements to human players
